pr.title: Use `BinOp::Cmp` for `iNN::signum`
pr.description: This way it can use the nice new LLVM intrinsic in LLVM20.
pr.author: scottmcm

processing.reason: The PR's rewrite of signed `iNN::signum` from the branch chain (`if self < 0 { -1 } else if self == 0 { 0 } else { 1 }`) to `crate::intrinsics::three_way_compare(self, 0) as Self` is value-equivalent for every signed integer input: both return -1, 0, or +1 for negative, zero, and positive values, including MIN/MAX. The `three_way_compare` intrinsic and its `LowerIntrinsics` lowering to `BinOp::Cmp` are also semantically the same three-way comparison. The only MIR-visible historical change besides the lowering is the unwind edge becoming `unwind unreachable` due to `#[rustc_nounwind]`, which is not a return-value miscompile and cannot produce differing defined observable values. Therefore no source-grounded original/transformed pair can be validated with distinct results; fabricating one would invent a non-historical wrong-result rewrite. This matches the frozen analysis's own conclusion that the PR is an optimization/cleanup, not a miscompile.

evidence: This way it can use the nice new LLVM intrinsic in LLVM20.
which must be of character or integer (signed or unsigned) type.
and then LLVM 20 added a backend intrinsic for it too.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical non-optimized transformation is the branch-chain implementation in `int_macros.rs` (`if self < 0 { -1 } else if self == 0 { 0 } else { 1 }`) rather than `three_way_compare(self, 0) as Self`. The patch replaces that expansion so `LowerIntrinsics` can produce `_3 = Cmp(move _4, move _5);`. Separately, before adding `#[rustc_nounwind]`, the lowered call was recorded as may-unwind (`unwind continue`); the corrected MIR expectation is `unwind unreachable`. This is an optimization gap, not evidence of a wrong-result miscompile.
analysis.inputDomain: `three_way_compare<T>` where T must be `char` or an integer type, signed or unsigned (`iNN`, `uNN`, `char`); `signum` applies to signed integer `iNN` with the fixed comparison operand `0` and returns the same integer type. Values to cover include negative, zero, and positive inputs, plus min/max boundary values.
analysis.originalLogic: Before the patch, `signum` for signed integers was a branch chain: `// FIXME(const-hack): replace with cmp` followed by `if self < 0 { -1 } else if self == 0 { 0 } else { 1 }`. This computes -1/0/+1 but emits multiple MIR comparisons and branches instead of a single three-way comparison. The `three_way_compare` intrinsic already lowered to `Cmp` in `LowerIntrinsics`, but `signum` did not use it.
pitfalls: Do not conflate the `Cmp` lowering with the unwind-edge change: the test diffs change `unwind continue` to `unwind unreachable` because of `#[rustc_nounwind]`, while the `Cmp` line is the LowerIntrinsics result.
The char and unsigned test diffs also change unwind behavior even though the PR title and source edit concern `iNN::signum`; the intrinsic attribute applies to all supported types.
The old comment `FIXME(const-hack): replace with cmp` and the branch chain are the pre-optimization form; the retained test names do not imply the old lowering was semantically wrong.
`signum` must still cast the `Ordering` result `as Self`; the intrinsic returns `crate::cmp::Ordering`, not the integer type.
Do not invent a different-result rewrite: the branch chain and `three_way_compare` agree on -1/0/+1 for signed values; the difference is MIR/LLVM form and unwind metadata.
preconditions: The intrinsic must be usable from a const fn, hence the added `rustc_intrinsic_const_stable_indirect`.
`three_way_compare` must be marked `rustc_nounwind` for its call edge to become `unwind unreachable`.
The operand type must be one of char, signed integer, or unsigned integer, as documented: `which must be of character or integer (signed or unsigned) type`.
`LowerIntrinsics` must be run to observe `Cmp`; without it the call remains `three_way_compare`.
analysis.summary: Optimization PR: make signed-integer `iNN::signum` call `intrinsics::three_way_compare(self, 0)` instead of a three-branch comparison, so `LowerIntrinsics` turns it into `BinOp::Cmp` and LLVM 20 can use its three-way-compare intrinsic. The same patch marks `three_way_compare` `rustc_nounwind`, so its lowered MIR call edge changes from `unwind continue` to `unwind unreachable` for all supported types (char, signed, unsigned). This is an optimization/cleanup, not a reported miscompile.
analysis.testStrategy: Use the MIR-opt `LowerIntrinsics` dump tests (`tests/mir-opt/lower_intrinsics.three_way_compare_{char,signed,unsigned}.*.diff`) to assert that `three_way_compare::<T>(...)` is replaced by `Cmp(...)` and that the call edge is `unwind unreachable` due to `rustc_nounwind`. Add focused `signum` runtime tests for signed integers at MIN, -1, 0, 1, and MAX, and a const-context test since the intrinsic is now const-stable-indirect. The two comparison programs for differential reasoning should differ only in the `signum` body: branch chain versus `three_way_compare(self, 0) as Self`.
analysis.trigger: When MIR contains a call to the `three_way_compare` intrinsic, `LowerIntrinsics` lowers it to the `Cmp` binary operation. This is now triggered by `iNN::signum` because it directly calls `crate::intrinsics::three_way_compare(self, 0) as Self` instead of expanding a branch chain. The intrinsic's `rustc_nounwind` annotation also makes the call's unwind edge unreachable.
